headline: Revenue surges on Legend deal as losses narrow
summary_short: Revenue rose 62% y/y to $269.9M, with Media revenue up 126% on the Legend acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA reached $87.1M and net loss narrowed to $15.7M.
summary_long: Betting Technology revenue grew 33% to $153.0M on contract price increases tied to official data rights and expanded services. Media Technology revenue rose to $116.9M, driven mainly by Legend. Cost of revenue rose $52.9M on acquired-intangible amortization, Legend staff and media costs, and data rights fees. Net interest expense was $19.1M against $0.1M a year ago after the Credit Agreement. Cash was $206.5M at September 30.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EBITDA is non-GAAP, taken from the company's reconciliation. Q3 2026 includes Legend, so y/y comparisons are not organic. Operating income and q/q revenue deltas use shard values (Yahoo timeseries); other figures from the 6-K interim report.

drivers.explanation: Betting revenue grew on renewal price increases and new services; Media revenue more than doubled, primarily driven by the Legend acquisition.
Interest, related fees and debt issuance cost amortization on the Credit Agreement, partly offset by interest income on cash.
Cost of revenue grew from higher intangible amortization, Legend-related staff and media costs, and data rights fees, while income tax moved to a $7.1M expense.
